result.title: Estimated energy performance
result.description: Based on the property information provided, this is an indicative estimate of your home's energy performance.
result.label: Estimated energy label
result.warning: This result is an indicative estimate and is not an official EPC or PEB certificate. An official energy rating can only be determined using the relevant regional certification method.

explanation.title: What does your EPC or PEB score mean?
explanation.description: The energy score indicates how efficiently a home performs under standardised conditions. It is expressed in kilowatt-hours of primary energy per square metre per year, or kWh/(m² year).
explanation.secondary: The lower the energy score, the more energy efficient the property. The calculation considers factors such as roof, wall and floor insulation, windows, heating, domestic hot water, ventilation and renewable energy.

score.title: A lower score means better energy performance
score.description: The score represents the calculated annual energy performance per square metre of the property. A home with a lower score generally requires less primary energy under the same standardised conditions.

label.title: The label makes the energy score easier to understand
label.description: The numerical energy score is converted into an energy label. Flanders, Brussels and Wallonia each use their own label scale and threshold values.

usage.title: Your EPC or PEB score is not the same as your energy bill
usage.description: Energy performance certificates use standardised assumptions so that homes can be compared fairly. Your actual energy consumption may be higher or lower depending on occupancy, heating behaviour and personal habits.

labels.title: Which energy score corresponds to which label?
labels.description: Energy label thresholds differ between Belgium's regions. See how EPC and PEB scores are classified in Flanders, Brussels and Wallonia.

flanders.title: EPC labels in Flanders
flanders.description: In Flanders, residential EPC labels range from A+ to F. A lower energy score indicates a more energy-efficient home.
flanders.note: The displayed thresholds follow the Flemish residential EPC label scale. Only an official EPC can determine the final label of a property.

brussels.title: PEB labels in Brussels
brussels.description: In the Brussels-Capital Region, the current residential PEB scale ranges from A to G.
brussels.note: Brussels uses its own PEB methodology and threshold values. A Flemish EPC score therefore cannot be directly interpreted as a Brussels PEB label.

wallonia.title: PEB labels in Wallonia
wallonia.description: Wallonia uses a residential PEB scale ranging from A++ to G, based on the theoretical specific primary energy consumption.
wallonia.note: Wallonia uses its own PEB calculation methodology and label scale. Only an official PEB certificate determines the final label.

improvements.title: How can you improve your home's energy rating?
improvements.description: Improving energy performance usually starts by reducing heat loss. Roof and external wall insulation can therefore play an important role in improving a home's calculated energy performance.

cavity.title: Cavity wall insulation
cavity.description: If your home has a suitable uninsulated cavity wall, cavity wall insulation can reduce heat loss through the external walls. Existing wall insulation is taken into account when assessing energy performance.

roof.title: Roof insulation
roof.description: An inadequately insulated roof can lead to significant heat loss. Depending on the property, either the roof itself or the attic floor can be insulated to improve the thermal envelope.

facade.title: External insulation with render
facade.description: When cavity wall insulation is not possible or sufficient, external wall insulation can provide an alternative. The insulation layer is combined with a new rendered façade finish.

other.title: Other parts of your home also affect the energy score
other.description: In addition to insulation, energy performance calculations also consider windows and doors, heating, domestic hot water, ventilation and renewable energy.

windows.title: Windows & glazing
windows.description: High-performance or triple glazing can reduce heat loss through windows, particularly where single glazing or older double glazing is still present.

heating.title: Heating
heating.description: The efficiency and type of heating system influence the calculated energy use of the property.

solar.title: Solar energy
solar.description: Solar panels and solar thermal systems can contribute to energy performance by supplying part of the home's energy from renewable sources.

improvements.note: The measure with the greatest impact varies from one property to another. An official EPC or PEB assessment and its recommendations provide more detailed information for the specific property.

indicative.title: Why is this EPC or PEB calculation an estimate?
indicative.description: Our calculator provides an initial estimate of a home's energy performance based on the information you enter. An official EPC or PEB assessment uses more detailed technical data and follows the certification methodology of the relevant region.

data.title: The information you provide
data.description: The calculation considers factors such as property type, construction year, floor area, insulation, glazing, heating, ventilation and renewable energy.

assumptions.title: Missing technical information is estimated
assumptions.description: When certain technical details are unknown, the calculator has to use assumptions. The actual official energy score may therefore differ from the estimate.

official.title: An official certificate requires an official assessment
official.description: Only an EPC or PEB certificate produced according to the relevant regional certification methodology can determine the official energy score and label.

notice.title: Important:
notice.description: use this result as an initial indication of your home's energy performance, not as an official EPC or PEB certificate.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions about EPC and PEB
faq.description: Find answers about energy scores, energy labels, our calculator and improving your home's energy performance.

hero.description: Calculate how much energy you could potentially save by improving your home's insulation. Enter a few details about your property and its current insulation to receive an indicative estimate of your annual energy savings.

calculator.title: Calculate your potential energy savings
calculator.description: Answer a few questions about your home, its current insulation and heating situation. You will then receive an indicative estimate of how much heating energy insulation could save.
calculator.error: The energy savings could not be calculated. Please try again.

result.title: Your estimated energy savings
result.description: Based on your property, current insulation, heating situation and selected insulation measure, you receive the indicative estimate below.
result.rangeDescription: Actual savings may vary depending on the property, the quality of the insulation work and your heating behaviour.
result.warning: This calculation is indicative and is not an energy audit or a guarantee of future energy consumption or energy costs. Actual savings depend on factors including the existing construction, quality of the insulation work, weather conditions, indoor temperature and heating behaviour.

calculator.disclaimer: This calculator provides an indicative estimate. Actual savings depend on factors such as the property, quality of installation, indoor temperature and heating behaviour.

building.title: Tell us about your home
building.description: A few basic details help us estimate the size of the property and its heating demand more accurately.

region.question: Which region is the property located in?

type.question: What type of property do you have?

insulation.title: How is your home currently insulated?
insulation.description: The existing insulation determines how much additional heat loss could potentially be reduced through new insulation work.

roof.question: How is the roof currently insulated?

walls.question: How are the external walls currently insulated?

measure.description: Select the insulation measure for which you would like an indication of the potential energy savings.

type.question: Which measure would you like to carry out?

surface.label: Estimated area to be insulated
surface.help: An estimate is sufficient. For walls, enter the approximate external façade area. For roof insulation, enter the roof or attic floor area to be insulated.

heating.title: How do you heat your home?
heating.description: Your heating system and current energy use help us estimate the potential savings more accurately.

source.question: What is your main heating source?

heating.help: Enter your annual energy consumption in kWh, which can usually be found on your annual energy statement. If you also enter your annual heating cost, we can estimate the potential financial saving.

explanation.title: How do we calculate your potential energy savings?
explanation.description: A home loses heat through areas such as the roof and external walls. Improving a poorly insulated building element can reduce that heat loss. Our calculator estimates the potential effect of the selected insulation measure for your situation.

current.title: Current situation
current.description: We first estimate the current heat loss based on factors including the construction year, existing insulation and the surface area of the building element.

improved.title: After insulation
improved.description: We then estimate how much the heat loss could decrease once the selected building element is better insulated.

result.title: Your estimated savings
result.description: The difference is converted into an indicative energy saving in kWh, a percentage and, when provided, an estimated financial saving.

factors.title: Which information do we use?
factors.description: The calculation takes several factors into account that can affect the potential impact of insulation.

explanation.notice: The calculation remains an indicative estimate. Actual energy savings may vary depending on factors such as the property's construction, quality of installation, weather conditions, indoor temperature and heating behaviour.

measures.title: Which types of insulation can help you save energy?
measures.description: Not every insulation measure has the same effect in every home. Potential savings mainly depend on how much heat the building element currently loses and how well it is already insulated.

cavity.title: Cavity wall insulation
cavity.description: Cavity wall insulation fills the space between the inner and outer wall with insulating material. This can reduce heat loss through external walls without having to renovate the entire façade.
cavity.suitable: The property has a suitable cavity wall that is empty or insufficiently insulated.

roof.title: Roof insulation
roof.description: Heat rises, so a poorly insulated roof can be an important source of heat loss. Roof or attic floor insulation helps keep more heat inside the heated part of the property.
roof.suitable: The roof is uninsulated, poorly insulated or contains older insulation.

facade.title: External wall insulation
facade.description: External wall insulation adds an insulating layer to the outside of the property. It can significantly reduce heat loss through external walls while also renewing the appearance of the façade.
facade.suitable: Cavity wall insulation is not possible or insufficient, or when the façade is already due for renovation.

cta.title: Which insulation method suits your home?
cta.description: Explore our insulation and façade solutions to discover which options could be suitable for your property.

factors.title: What determines your actual energy savings?
factors.description: The calculator provides an estimate. Two homes with the same floor area can still achieve different savings in practice because several technical and behavioural factors affect energy use.

important.title: A calculation remains an estimate
important.description: The calculator compares an estimated current situation with an improved situation after insulation. An exact assessment requires information such as the actual construction, insulation thickness and condition of the property.

existingInsulation.title: Existing insulation
existingInsulation.description: The poorer the current insulation of a roof or external wall, the greater the potential reduction in heat loss will generally be.

construction.title: Construction year and structure
construction.description: The construction of the walls, roof and other building elements affects how much heat the property loses and how much improvement additional insulation can provide.

surface.title: Area to be insulated
surface.description: The size of the roof or external walls being insulated directly affects the amount of heat loss that can potentially be reduced.

heating.title: Heating system
heating.description: The type and efficiency of the heating system affect how much purchased energy is required to provide the same amount of heat inside the property.

temperature.title: Indoor temperature and weather
temperature.description: Higher indoor temperatures and colder outdoor conditions increase the temperature difference between inside and outside and therefore increase heat loss.

behaviour.title: Heating behaviour
behaviour.description: How long you heat the property, which rooms are heated and how the thermostat is used all influence the final energy consumption.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions about energy savings from insulation

metadata.description: Take the free Nu-Isoleren home check and discover which insulation, façade and moisture solutions may be suitable for your property.

hero.title: What insulation does your home need?
hero.description: Answer a few short questions about your property, roof, external walls, façade and any moisture problems. You will then receive a personalised overview of the Nu-Isoleren solutions that may be relevant for your home.
hero.disclaimer: The home check provides an initial indication and does not replace a technical inspection on site.

check.title: Discover which solutions may suit your home
check.description: Answer four short steps about your property, roof, external walls and any moisture problems. We will then show which Nu-Isoleren solutions may be relevant for your home.
check.disclaimer: This home check provides an initial indication based on your answers and does not replace an on-site technical inspection.

building.title: Tell us about your property
building.description: The construction year and property type provide an initial indication of the possible construction and insulation of your home.

region.question: Which region is your property located in?

type.question: What type of property do you have?

year.label: What year was the property built?

roof.title: How is your roof insulated?
roof.description: A roof with little or no insulation can be an important source of heat loss.

insulation.question: Which situation best describes your roof?

walls.title: What is the condition of your external walls and façade?
walls.description: We check whether cavity wall insulation, external wall insulation or a façade treatment may be relevant.

cavity.question: Does your property have cavity walls?

cavityInsulation.question: How is the cavity currently insulated?

facade.question: How would you describe the condition of the external façade?

moisture.title: Do you have moisture problems?
moisture.description: Some moisture problems should be correctly diagnosed before additional insulation or renovation work is carried out.

status.question: Which situation best matches your home?

options.rising: Damp patches at the bottom of walls

result.title: These solutions may be relevant for your property
result.description: Based on your answers, we have matched possible areas of concern in your property with solutions offered by Nu-Isoleren.

roof_insulation.title: Roof insulation
roof_insulation.description: Your answers suggest that your roof is not insulated, has limited insulation or may be insufficiently insulated. Improving the roof insulation can reduce heat loss and improve indoor comfort.
roof_insulation.nuIsoleren: Nu-Isoleren installs roof insulation using solutions including glass wool and PIR insulation boards.

cavity_wall_insulation.title: Cavity wall insulation
cavity_wall_insulation.description: Your property may have a cavity that is not or insufficiently insulated. If the cavity is technically suitable, insulating it can reduce heat loss through the external walls.
cavity_wall_insulation.nuIsoleren: Nu-Isoleren insulates suitable cavity walls using high-quality EPS beads.

cavity_cleaning.title: Cavity wall cleaning
cavity_cleaning.description: You indicated that old or potentially problematic insulation is present in the cavity. In some situations this should first be removed before new cavity wall insulation is installed.
cavity_cleaning.nuIsoleren: Nu-Isoleren removes old insulation and prepares the cavity for a new insulation solution.

external_wall_insulation.title: External wall insulation with render
external_wall_insulation.description: When cavity wall insulation is not possible or is insufficient, external wall insulation may be an alternative. The property is insulated from the outside and the façade is given a new finish.
external_wall_insulation.nuIsoleren: Nu-Isoleren installs external insulation boards and finishes the façade with render.

facade_cleaning.title: Façade cleaning
facade_cleaning.description: Your façade appears to be mainly affected by dirt or deposits. Professional cleaning can remove contamination and help restore the appearance of the exterior walls.
facade_cleaning.nuIsoleren: Nu-Isoleren professionally cleans exterior façades using a method suited to the surface.

hydrofuge.title: Water-repellent façade treatment
hydrofuge.description: A damp or porous façade can absorb rainwater more easily. Once the cause has been assessed, a water-repellent treatment may help protect the exterior wall against weather exposure.
hydrofuge.nuIsoleren: Nu-Isoleren applies hydrofuge treatment to suitable façades to make the exterior surface water repellent.

rising_damp.title: Rising damp treatment
rising_damp.description: Damp patches at the bottom of internal walls can indicate rising damp. Mould or damaged plaster can also have other causes, so an on-site inspection is important.
rising_damp.nuIsoleren: Nu-Isoleren treats rising damp by injecting the walls with an appropriate damp-proofing product.

noRecommendations.title: No obvious issues detected
noRecommendations.description: Based on your answers, we did not identify a direct insulation or moisture problem for which we can make a clear recommendation. An on-site inspection can provide more certainty if required.

result.notice: This home check is indicative. The technical condition of a roof, cavity wall, façade or moisture problem can only be assessed correctly through an on-site inspection.

advice.title: From home check to the right solution
advice.description: Every property is different. The home check helps identify possible areas of concern and links them to solutions that Nu-Isoleren can carry out.

points.check: Based on your answers, you receive an initial indication of possible insulation, façade or moisture issues.
points.solution: The home check directly links these points of attention to suitable Nu-Isoleren services.
points.inspection: If required, the technical situation can be assessed on site before determining the final solution.

advice.notice: An online home check cannot assess every detail of a property. The condition of the cavity walls, roof, façade and any moisture issues can be evaluated more accurately during an on-site inspection.

metadata.title: Insulation Grants Flanders 2026 & 2027 | Nu-Isoleren
metadata.description: Discover the current insulation grants available in Flanders in 2026, including Mijn VerbouwPremie for roof insulation and external wall insulation. View grant amounts, eligibility conditions and changes for 2027.

hero.title: Insulation grants in Flanders in 2026
hero.description: Homeowners who insulate their property may, in certain situations, qualify for Mijn VerbouwPremie. The rules changed on 1 March 2026. Find out below who is still eligible, which insulation works are supported and how much financial support may be available.

update.title: How much is Mijn VerbouwPremie for insulation?
update.description: Since 1 March 2026, owner-occupiers in income categories 1 and 2 are no longer eligible for Mijn VerbouwPremie for these insulation works. Financial support remains available for income categories 3 and 4.
update.notice: The amounts above are maximum grant amounts. The final amount depends on the eligible invoice, your income category and the applicable Mijn VerbouwPremie conditions. The application date determines which scheme applies.

intro.title: What is Mijn VerbouwPremie?
intro.description: Mijn VerbouwPremie is a grant provided by the Flemish government for renovation work and energy-saving investments in houses and apartments located in the Flemish Region.
intro.descriptionSecond: For Nu-Isoleren, the most relevant categories are roof and external wall works. These include roof insulation, cavity wall insulation and external façade insulation.
intro.highlight: Eligibility depends on factors such as your income category, the type of property, the work carried out and the applicable technical conditions.
intro.imageAlt: Home in Flanders during energy renovation and insulation work

eligibility.title: Who qualifies for an insulation grant?
eligibility.description: For applications submitted from 1 March 2026, owner-occupiers in income categories 3 and 4 remain eligible for Mijn VerbouwPremie for roof and wall insulation.

points.building: The house or apartment must be located in the Flemish Region and must have been connected to the electricity distribution network before 1 January 2006, or first occupied before that date according to cadastral records.
points.income: Your income category is determined using the most recently available tax assessment at the time of application.
points.property: An owner-occupier who also fully owns another house, apartment or building plot is automatically placed in income category 1.

table.notice: These income thresholds apply to applications submitted from 1 January 2026.

works.title: Which insulation works are eligible?
works.description: Mijn VerbouwPremie applies specific technical requirements to each type of insulation work. For Nu-Isoleren, roof insulation, cavity wall insulation and external wall insulation are the most relevant.

roof.title: Roof insulation
roof.description: New roof or attic-floor insulation may qualify when it meets the technical requirements of the scheme.
roof.requirement1: The newly installed insulation must achieve an Rd value of at least 4.5 m²K/W.
roof.requirement2: When insulating a pitched roof from the inside, a correctly installed vapour barrier is required.

cavity.title: Cavity wall insulation
cavity.description: Insulating a suitable existing cavity wall falls under the external wall category.
cavity.requirement1: The cavity must be completely filled, be at least 50 mm wide and the insulation material must have a maximum lambda value of 0.065 W/mK.
cavity.requirement2: The work must be carried out by an STS 71-1 recognised contractor. A cavity that is already partially insulated does not qualify for additional filling.

facade.title: External wall insulation
facade.description: Insulating an external wall from the outside may also qualify, including façade renovation combined with insulation and render.
facade.requirement1: New external wall insulation must achieve an Rd value of at least 3 m²K/W.
facade.requirement2: Façade finishes such as render are only eligible when combined with sufficient new external wall insulation.

works.notice: The insulation work must meet all technical and administrative requirements applicable at the time of the grant application.

application.title: How do you apply for Mijn VerbouwPremie?
application.description: The grant application is submitted after the work has been completed and the required invoices and certificates are available.

works.title: Have the insulation work completed
works.description: Roof and external wall insulation must be carried out by a contractor. Certain techniques require additional contractor certification.

documents.title: Collect your invoices and certificates
documents.description: Keep the final invoice, any advance or interim invoices and the required contractor certificate. Cavity wall insulation also requires the STS 71-1 VVO certificate.

portal.title: Apply through Mijn VerbouwLoket
portal.description: Mijn VerbouwPremie is applied for online through Mijn VerbouwLoket, with a separate application for each category of work.

followup.title: Track your application
followup.description: After submission, you can follow the application through Mijn VerbouwLoket. The authorities may request additional supporting documents.

application.notice: Invoices may be no more than 2 years old on the date the grant application is submitted.

future.title: What may change in 2027?
future.description: The Flemish Government is preparing an extension of Mijn VerbouwPremie for certain private landlords who rent their property under affordability conditions. They could become eligible for a 35% grant rate, comparable to income category 3.
future.social: An additional bonus has also been announced for certain landlords who rent their property through a housing company for at least nine years.
future.warning: As of September 2026, these changes had not yet been finally approved. Nu-Isoleren will update this page once the definitive rules are published.

metadata.title: Insulation Grants Brussels 2026 & 2027 | RENOLUTION & ECORENO
metadata.description: View the current status of insulation grants in Brussels in 2026 and 2027, including RENOLUTION, the ECORENO Credit and other renovation support.

hero.title: Insulation grants in Brussels in 2026
hero.description: The situation regarding renovation and insulation grants in the Brussels-Capital Region is unusual in 2026. Find out the current status of RENOLUTION Grants and which other forms of renovation support are currently available.
hero.imageAlt: Homes in Brussels suitable for energy renovation

status.title: No RENOLUTION applications for final invoices dated 2025 or 2026
status.description: According to the Brussels-Capital Region, no government decision has yet been taken regarding possible RENOLUTION Grants for 2025 and 2026.
status.highlight: At present, RENOLUTION Grant applications cannot be submitted for work with a final invoice dated in 2025 or 2026.
status.notice: Grant amounts and conditions from previous RENOLUTION schemes, such as the 2024 scheme, should therefore not be treated as current grant information for 2026.

renolution.title: What are RENOLUTION Grants?
renolution.description: Since 1 January 2022, RENOLUTION has been the name of the Brussels scheme combining the former Energy Grants, home renovation grants and façade improvement grants.
renolution.descriptionSecond: The scheme covered a range of renovation and energy-efficiency work, including insulation. However, there is currently no new grant scheme available for applications based on final invoices dated in 2025 or 2026.
renolution.highlight: Renovation work in Brussels should therefore not be planned on the basis of old RENOLUTION amounts without first checking the current official situation.
renolution.imageAlt: Energy renovation of a home in the Brussels-Capital Region

support.title: What renovation support is currently available?
support.description: The absence of a current RENOLUTION grant scheme does not mean that no financial support is available. Depending on your situation, other forms of assistance or financing may apply.

ecoreno.title: ECORENO Credit
ecoreno.description: A financing solution for renovation work on a home in the Brussels-Capital Region, including work intended to improve energy performance.

municipal.title: Municipal support
municipal.description: Some Brussels municipalities provide their own grants or financial incentives. Availability and eligibility conditions vary between municipalities.

vat.title: Reduced 6% VAT
vat.description: Certain renovation work may qualify for the reduced 6% VAT rate when the legal conditions are met. This is a tax benefit rather than a RENOLUTION Grant.

support.notice: The support available to you depends on factors including the type of property, your status, your household income and the work being planned.

ecoreno.title: Financing renovation work with the ECORENO Credit
ecoreno.description: The ECORENO Credit provides a financing solution for various renovation works on homes located in Brussels.
ecoreno.notGrant: ECORENO is a loan, not a renovation grant.

rate.label: Interest rate
rate.value: Preferential interest rate of 2.5% to 3.5%, depending on the applicable conditions and household income thresholds.

applicants.label: Who can apply?
applicants.value: Owners, future owners and tenants of a home in the Brussels-Capital Region may qualify subject to the applicable conditions.

works.label: Which work?
works.value: This includes conventional renovation work, energy-performance improvements, safety, health and habitability improvements and certain adaptations relating to personal autonomy.

contractor.label: Execution
contractor.value: The work must be carried out by a professional contractor who meets the applicable registration and professional requirements.

ecoreno.notice: According to the current information from Homegrade, the ECORENO Credit is not currently available to landlord-owners or associations of co-owners. Additional financial and administrative conditions also apply.

future.title: What do we know about Brussels grants in 2027?
future.description: For 2027, we will only publish specific grant amounts and eligibility conditions once they have been officially established by the Brussels-Capital Region.
future.descriptionSecond: As of September 2026, no definitive 2027 RENOLUTION scheme has been published that provides reliable insulation grant amounts.
future.warning: Nu-Isoleren deliberately does not present old grant amounts or estimates as if they apply in 2027. This page will be updated when new official rules are published.

sources.title: Sources & latest information
sources.description: This page was reviewed in September 2026 using current information from the Brussels-Capital Region and Homegrade. Schemes and eligibility conditions may change.

metadata.title: Insulation Grants Wallonia 2026 & 2027 | Nu-Isoleren
metadata.description: View the current insulation grants in Wallonia in 2026 and the new renovation support scheme from 1 October 2026, including Rénopack and Rénoprêt.

hero.title: Insulation grants in Wallonia in 2026
hero.description: Renovation support in Wallonia changes significantly in 2026. The temporary Primes Habitation scheme ends on 30 September 2026 and is replaced from 1 October by a new system based on Rénopack and Rénoprêt.
hero.imageAlt: Home in Wallonia undergoing energy renovation work

transition.title: Walloon renovation support changes on 1 October 2026
transition.description: In September 2026, two different systems need to be distinguished. Which scheme applies depends on when the renovation project and application take place.

current.title: Primes Habitation 2025-2026
current.description: The temporary grant scheme remains applicable until 30 September 2026 inclusive. The grant application, including the final invoice, must be submitted no later than that date.

new.title: New renovation support scheme
new.description: Regional support will shift to Rénopack and Rénoprêt. The system will target energy-intensive homes where renovation results in a sufficient improvement of the PEB energy rating.

transition.notice: The per-square-metre amounts below apply only to the temporary scheme ending on 30 September 2026 and should not be treated as grant amounts under the new scheme.

currentPremiums.title: How much is the current insulation grant in Wallonia?
currentPremiums.description: Under the temporary scheme, a base grant amount is multiplied according to household income category. The figures below cover work relevant to Nu-Isoleren's services.
currentPremiums.notice: For income categories R1 and R2, the grant is limited to a maximum of 70% of the VAT-inclusive eligible invoice amount. For R3 and R4, the maximum is 50%. Higher base amounts exist for certain bio-based insulation materials.

eligibility.title: Who can still qualify for Primes Habitation?
eligibility.description: The temporary scheme includes conditions relating to the applicant, the property and how the work is carried out.

points.location: The property must be located in the Walloon Region, outside the territory of the German-speaking Community.
points.age: The building must be more than 15 years old.
points.usage: More than 50% of the building must be or become residential.
points.contractor: The work must be carried out by a contractor registered with the Crossroads Bank for Enterprises and, where required, holding the necessary professional access.
points.audit: A prior Housing Audit is required for most renovation work. It is not mandatory for roof work or thermal insulation of the roof or attic.

eligibility.imageAlt: Energy renovation of a home in Wallonia

newRegime.title: How will the new Walloon renovation scheme work?
newRegime.description: From 1 October 2026, support will focus on homes with poor energy performance. The renovation project must result in a sufficient improvement in the property's PEB rating.

gf.label: PEB F or G
gf.value: The renovation must improve the property to at least PEB rating D.

e.label: PEB E
e.value: The renovation must improve the property to at least PEB rating C.

newRegime.audit: A prior audit will be mandatory to access the new financing. Support will be calculated across the overall renovation project rather than separately for each type of insulation work.

loans.title: What financial support applies from October 2026?
loans.description: Walloon support will be structured around two renovation loans. Household income category determines which financing system and repayment reduction applies.

renopack.title: Rénopack
renopack.description: For C1, C2 and C3 households. It is a zero-interest renovation loan combined with a reduction in the amount that ultimately has to be repaid.

renopret.title: Rénoprêt
renopret.description: For C4 households, landlord-owners and associations of co-owners. The interest rate depends on the applicable conditions and is preferential compared with normal market financing.

loans.notice: For a single-family home, financing may reach €75,000. According to the Walloon authorities, the official reduction percentages for C1, C2 and C3 include the possible 5% increase for the use of eco-materials. Income thresholds are indexed as of 1 January 2026.

application.title: Which procedure applies to your renovation?
application.description: Because the scheme changes on 1 October 2026, the first step is to determine which system your renovation project falls under.

before.title: Until 30 September 2026
before.description: Applications under the temporary Primes Habitation scheme must be submitted by 30 September 2026 at the latest, including the final invoice. Applications can be made through Mon Espace or using the official forms.

after.title: From 1 October 2026
after.description: New projects will fall under the Rénopack and Rénoprêt system. A prior audit will be mandatory and the overall project must meet the applicable PEB improvement and financing conditions.

sources.title: Sources & latest information
sources.description: This page was reviewed in September 2026 using official information from the Walloon authorities. The transition to the new scheme is scheduled for 1 October 2026 and administrative details may continue to be clarified.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.description: How Nu-Isoleren.be processes personal data when you use this website or submit an enquiry.

sections.title: Who handles your data?
sections.text: Nu-Isoleren.be BV is the controller of personal data collected through this website. For questions about your data or to exercise your rights, contact us using the email address, telephone number or postal address above.

sections.title: Contact and quote requests
sections.text:
The contact form collects your first and last name, email address, optional phone number and message. A quote request also requires a phone number, street, house number, postcode, town and selected services; its message is optional. Both forms record the language and the time you confirm the privacy checkbox. Contact requests also store the source “contact_page”.
Requests are stored in the backend database with creation/update timestamps and a handling status. Quotes receive a reference and links to selected services. Contact requests may have internal follow-up notes. Neither form offers file uploads. Required fields are needed to submit the form.

sections.title: Purposes and legal bases
sections.text:
We use your request to reply, contact you, assess the proposed work and prepare a quote. Quotes and enquiries made with a view to entering a contract involve steps taken at your request before a contract is concluded. The basis for other enquiries and technical logging still needs to be documented; we do not assume blanket consent for all processing.
The required privacy checkbox records your confirmation, not permission for advertising or a newsletter. Optional marketing technology has a separate consent choice. You may withdraw consent to processing that relies on it.

sections.title: Hosting, storage and email
sections.text:
Vercel hosts the frontend; the Laravel backend and database are managed through Laravel Cloud. Brevo provides transactional email: internal contact notifications, and internal notifications and customer confirmations for quotes. Messages may include the request details, your name and email address. Form success confirms database receipt, not email delivery.
Website images use configurable object storage; its final provider and region remain to be confirmed. An optional CRM webhook exists for quote follow-up. Its activation and recipient must be checked before it is described as an active transfer.

sections.title: Technical data and security
sections.text: Delivering pages and processing requests sends connection information, including your IP address, to the relevant servers. The backend validates input, limits requests and logs errors. External service error responses may appear in logs. Production log fields, access permissions and retention are not yet fully established. This website does not place form data in thank-you page URLs. This does not guarantee the practices of every external provider.

sections.title: Google, Meta and embedded content
sections.text:
Google Tag Manager manages Google Ads and Meta Pixel. The marketing agency does not currently use Google Analytics. The site passes analytics and marketing preferences to the container; whether every tag respects them must be checked in GTM. The forms do not themselves send names, email addresses or other form fields to the dataLayer.
Google Places supplies business reviews through the server; reviewer photos may load from Google. The contact page includes a Google Maps iframe which is currently not blocked by cookie preferences. Google receives connection information when it loads. See also our cookie policy.

sections.title: International transfers
sections.text: International providers may process data outside the European Economic Area. Specific regions, recipients and applicable transfer safeguards have not yet been confirmed. We therefore do not claim any particular adequacy arrangement or contractual safeguard. Contact us for information about your data; these details need to be completed before production readiness is finalised.

sections.title: Retention
sections.text:
Ordinary leads and contact enquiries that do not result in a customer relationship: at most 2 years after the last contact.

Quote requests that do not result in a customer relationship: at most 2 years after the last contact.

When a prospect becomes a customer, personal data needed to perform the contract, handle administration, keep accounts, issue invoices or meet legal obligations may be retained longer in accordance with the applicable statutory retention periods. This does not mean that all earlier prospect data automatically remains necessary.

Belgian accounting and tax documents must generally be retained for 10 years, subject to the applicable rules and any exceptions. This statutory document-retention obligation is separate from the period for ordinary contact enquiries and quote requests without a customer relationship.

Cookie consent (nu-isoleren.consent) remains valid for at most 180 days, as technically configured. The site then asks for your choice again.

Separate periods for technical logs, backups and storage by external providers still need to be established. The contact and quote retention periods above are company policy; practical deletion procedures must be aligned with that policy.

sections.title: Your rights and withdrawing consent
sections.text: Subject to the applicable conditions, you may request access, correction, erasure, restriction or portability of your data and object to processing. Use the contact details above. Clarification or proportionate identity verification may be needed. Withdrawing consent does not affect the lawfulness of earlier processing based on consent. Change cookie preferences using the button below or in the footer. You may also complain to the Belgian Data Protection Authority using the link below.

cookies.title: Cookie policy
cookies.description: Cookies and similar technologies on this website and how to manage your preferences.

sections.title: Cookies and similar storage
sections.text: Cookies are small pieces of data stored by your browser and potentially sent with matching requests. localStorage keeps data in your browser without automatically sending it with every request. Tags, pixels and iframes may also contact external services.

sections.title: Necessary storage
sections.text:
nu-isoleren.consent is this site’s localStorage item. It stores necessary, analytics and marketing choices, the consent version and saved/expiry timestamps. A choice is valid for at most 180 days. Afterwards it is no longer applied and the banner appears again; localStorage does not automatically physically delete the old value. Necessary storage remains active.
NEXT_LOCALE is the next-intl language cookie, saved when needed. The current configuration sets no max-age: it is a session cookie, whose restoration also depends on browser settings. No other application-owned sessionStorage use was identified.

sections.title: Analytics
sections.text: Analytics is off by default and reserved for optional statistics services. The marketing agency does not currently use Google Analytics. An analytics choice is not marketing consent and does not itself load a separate Analytics script in this site.

sections.title: Marketing: Google Ads and Meta Pixel
sections.text: Google Ads and Meta Pixel are managed through GTM, not separate website scripts. Marketing is off by default. With consent these services can measure campaigns and conversions, including visits to contact or quote thank-you pages. Exact tags, cookies, recipients, individual purposes and lifetimes still need checking in the external container and production browser. We do not publish an unverified cookie list.

sections.title: Google Tag Manager and Consent Mode v2
sections.text:
GTM-P6K3L9WQ loads after the site first sets analytics_storage, ad_storage, ad_user_data and ad_personalization to denied and processes any valid stored choice. Analytics controls analytics_storage; marketing controls the three advertising values. Changes are sent through Consent Mode and nu_consent_update.
GTM may load while denied. Depending on settings, Google tags can send cookieless measurement requests. Meta tags require their own GTM restrictions; Consent Mode does not automatically block every tag. Without JavaScript, the noscript iframe may contact Google but cannot read localStorage preferences. This fallback must not run optional tags; its container settings need checking.

sections.title: Google Maps and reviews
sections.text: The contact-page Maps iframe currently loads directly when the browser loads it, independently of cookie preferences. Google may receive technical data and use its own storage. Exact cookies and durations have not been established. Google Places supplies reviews through our server; external reviewer photos may also make requests to Google. These services are not described as already consent-gated.

sections.title: Accepting, rejecting and changing preferences
sections.text:
On your first visit you can reject all, set preferences or accept all. Analytics and marketing can be chosen independently. “Cookie preferences” in the footer or below lets you change or withdraw your choice. Missing, invalid, expired or outdated-version preferences cause the banner to appear again.
Clearing browser storage also clears your choice. Withdrawal changes future permission but does not automatically remove cookies or data already held by external providers. Use browser settings where necessary and contact us to exercise your privacy rights.

sections.title: External storage still to verify
sections.text: The GTM container contents and providers’ production settings are outside this website code. Specific names, domains, lifetimes and transfers will be added only after reliable verification. See the privacy policy for contact details, data processing and your rights.
